video_summary: This video introduces Node.js, explaining what it is, how it was created, and why it exists. The instructor breaks down how JavaScript traditionally runs inside browsers using JavaScript engines like V8, and explains how Ryan Dahl combined Chrome's V8 engine with C++ to create Node.js. The lecture demonstrates running JavaScript code in Chrome DevTools versus the Node.js terminal REPL, concluding with the official definition of Node.js as an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment.

sections.title: Understanding JavaScript & JS Engines
spoken_content: JavaScript was originally designed as a client-side scripting language executed strictly inside web browsers to make web pages interactive.
Browsers cannot run JavaScript directly without a specialized component called a JavaScript Engine.
When a user downloads and uses a web browser, the JavaScript Engine comes embedded with it to execute JS scripts.
Different web browsers rely on different JS engines: Chrome uses Google's V8 engine, Firefox uses SpiderMonkey, and Safari uses Apple's JavaScriptCore.
Among all JavaScript engines, Google Chrome's V8 engine is the most popular and widely used.

sections.title: Creation of Node.js and Core Capabilities
spoken_content: Developer Ryan Dahl created Node.js by taking Chrome's open-source V8 JavaScript engine and embedding it inside C++ code.
By binding V8 with C++, JavaScript gained the ability to execute outside the web browser environment.

Since C++ interacts natively with machine hardware and operating systems, Node.js enables JavaScript to perform machine-level operations such as file system handling, file access, and memory management.
This architectural setup allows developers to write backend server-side applications and web servers entirely in JavaScript.

sections.title: Defining Node.js & Practical Demonstration
spoken_content: Node.js is neither a programming language, nor a framework, nor a library; it is a JavaScript Runtime Environment.
In a browser, JavaScript runs within the browser console via the embedded V8 engine.
In the OS terminal, attempting to run raw JavaScript commands directly results in a syntax error because standard terminal shells lack a JS interpreter.
By launching the Node.js REPL (`node`), an interactive environment opens where JavaScript code can be typed and executed directly on the host operating system.

sections.title: Official Node.js Definition & Prerequisites
spoken_content: The official definition on nodejs.org states: 'Node.js is an open-source, cross-platform JavaScript runtime environment.'
Because Node.js is simply an execution environment, developers write pure JavaScript code inside it.
Having a strong foundation in core JavaScript concepts is an absolute prerequisite before starting to build applications with Node.js.
